ordered_diagnoses: Myocardial Infarction with Non-Obstructive Coronary Arteries

facts.raw_span: A 67-year-old man
hypertension, dyslipidaemia, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, active smoking (35 pack-years), a family history of ischaemic heart disease
prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina
exercise stress test induced angina at 50 W without ECG changes
normal sinus rhythm, Q waves in lead III, and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF
left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities
patent stents in the circumflex artery, non-significant disease in the left anterior descending artery, and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3
subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch
recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
new QTc prolongation to 500 ms
A 67-year-old man
hypertension, dyslipidaemia, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, active smoking (35 pack-years), a family history of ischaemic heart disease
prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina
exercise stress test induced angina at 50 W without ECG changes
normal sinus rhythm, Q waves in lead III, and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF
left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities
patent stents in the circumflex artery, non-significant disease in the left anterior descending artery, and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3
subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch
recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
new QTc prolongation to 500 ms

concepts.why: The patient has a history of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction, prior percutaneous coronary interventions, and currently presents with Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina and ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3.

The patient developed akinesia of all apical segments, later extending to mid-segments, hyperkinesia of the basal segments, and severely reduced LVEF of 35%, which is consistent with takotsubo syndrome, especially given the presence of new QTc prolongation and recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.

concepts.preferred_label: Myocardial Infarction with Non-Obstructive Coronary Arteries
concepts.why: The patient has a history of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction and currently presents with ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3, but coronary angiography demonstrated patent stents and non-significant disease in the left anterior descending artery.

The patient has a history of prior percutaneous coronary interventions and currently presents with significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis and subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch.
The patient developed recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation requiring external shocks and cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

rationales.F02: Hypertension and dyslipidaemia increase the risk of atherosclerosis, which is a key factor in acute coronary syndrome.
rationales.F03: Prior percutaneous coronary interventions suggest a history of coronary artery disease, which increases the risk of restenosis.
rationales.F08: Significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis is a strong indicator of acute coronary syndrome and coronary artery restenosis.
rationales.F09: ST-segment elevation is a key indicator of myocardial infarction, but the absence of regional wall-motion abnormalities on echocardiography makes myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries less likely.
rationales.F10: Subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch is a strong indicator of coronary artery restenosis.
rationales.F11: Recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia is a strong indicator of ventricular tachycardia.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with worsening chest pain, ST-segment elevation, and subsequent development of akinesia of all apical segments with severely reduced LVEF, despite the presence of coronary artery disease, is more consistent with Takotsubo Syndrome, especially given the presence of emotional distress (anxiety) and the unique echocardiographic findings.
